raw_response:
My family has farmed this land in Quzhou my whole life. I'm 64 now and my son helps when he can, but mostly it's me. I have about 8 mu. I'm not going to experiment at my age — wheat and corn, same as always, same as my father. That's what this land knows and what I know.

For winter wheat, I'll plant in October after the corn is off. I'll plough the field properly — I don't trust this no-till business the extension office keeps pushing. I buy Jimai improved seed from the village supply store. Been using it for years. I'll put down compound fertilizer at planting and top-dress with urea at green-up and jointing. I always do the winter irrigation in November before the ground freezes, then water again at jointing and at heading — three times. Aphids get bad in May so I spray twice, once for weeds in autumn, once for disease and insects in spring. I expect around 480 jin per mu if weather cooperates.

After wheat harvest in June I go straight to corn. No time to waste. I use Zhengdan 958 hybrid — reliable, everyone around here uses it. Rotary till after the wheat stubble, plant the same day. Corn mostly gets rain in July and August but I'll pump groundwater once if it's dry. One pesticide pass for corn borer. Pull it in late September.
